sentences: The deadliest wave in Boston's history wasn't water.
It was molasses.
January fifteenth nineteen nineteen.
Just after noon in the North End.
A fifty-foot steel tank holds two point three million gallons.
The day is unusually warm.
Then rivets pop like gunfire.
And the tank splits open.
Molasses is forty percent heavier than water.
So it doesn't ooze.
It surges.
A wave up to twenty-five feet high races at thirty-five miles an hour.
It flattens buildings and bends the elevated railway.
Twenty-one people die.
A hundred and fifty are hurt.
For decades locals said the streets still smelled sweet.
Then Boston changed its building rules.
Engineers had to show their math.
Slow as molasses?
Not that day.
